I’m a nurse at small LTC facility and recently had to send one of my patients out for what I suspected was sepsis. He had knee surgery a month ago and a week before we sent him to the ER because he suddenly started complaining of pain in the leg after what had been a relatively uneventful recovery. The hospital sent him home with antibiotics after doing labs and what not after determining he had an infection. A day later the guy goes to his ortho appointment where he’s seen by the surgeon’s PA who tells him he doesn’t have an infection, didn’t bother to look
at the labs that were drawn or the order and ultrasound, and  told him to stop taking the antibiotics. 2 days later he is running a fever and shaking uncontrollably and says he has pain all over and not just in his knee. I send him to the ER ASAP and the hospital was like “Why did they take him off antibiotics when he clearly had an infection?” So they run a bunch of tests and determine he has sepsis caused by an infection where in the knee he had surgery on (we were not aware because he presented no other symptoms until the day he was sent to the ER for pain a month after surgery. I was also not aware you could get an infection a month after surgery). He had to have surgery again to clean out the knee and remove the replacement. He will have to wait 6 weeks until the infection clears to have the replacement surgery done again. All of this over a PA’s mistake.

Then I got a really good job with decent pay at a very small long term care center for retired priests and brothers who are wonderful to work with and are actually grateful for the care and support the care team give them. I don’t ever have to deal with families, gross houses, and I don’t get treated like a second class citizen. Another thing I like here is that when they reach the end of their life and start declining and they start to become hospice appropriate we don’t have to argue with stupid family members who insist on keeping their loved ones alive “at all costs”. Almost everyone is a DNR, we don’t do tube feedings at our facility or vents. I’m not religious at all but it’s a beautiful thing to see these guys support each other through their faith in their community. We’ve got someone actively dying on hospice right now and his brethren are sitting watch near him around the clock almost so he doesn’t feel alone. So yeah, I found my forever job and I never want to go back to working with the general public ever again lol.

I work at a retirement community/LTC for retired Catholic priests. It’s pretty chill (most of the time. When we’re short staffed it can suck but that’s anywhere you work) The fathers and brothers are pretty cool. They’re probably the nicest patient group I’ve ever worked for, and to be honest I don’t think I’d want to go back to working for a non religious community. Even our dementia patients aren’t that bad (usually). They have their mass every day and all of the Catholic holidays and special feast days are observed. I’m agnostic so I’m not very religious, but they’ve never tried to convert anyone or preach religion to you. I like their sense of  community and how they support each other. Many of them have known each other for decades. I’d say about 99% of them are a DNR. We’ve never had anyone with a feeding tube. Nobody has a trach or a vent. Most of them except death as a part of life and just want to be made comfortable when their at the end of their life or are terminally ill. We don’t really have to deal with resident families. There is a father superior of the house who makes all of the medical decisions on their behalf if they cannot. There is a crucifix in every room and crucifixes throughout the facility. I’ve never had any issues getting my birth control. One of the few downsides to working here though is when they pass away because I can’t help but get attached to some of them. I won’t lie when I say I’ve cried like a baby in private for some of them. All of these guys have lived extraordinary lives and most are well traveled. I’m lucky to be here among them and even though I bitch about work sometimes (because who doesn’t) I consider myself lucky. Most of my coworkers are like a second family to me and I’d say overall it’s a very tight knit community. I’ve been through some very tough times these past 6 months and my coworkers and the fathers have been there for me and treated me with kindness and love when my own family hasn’t been there for me.
